items.stem: Describe how HIV infects the human body and causes AIDS. How is AIDS diagnosed, and how can its spread be prevented?
items.answer: HIV enters macrophages, where its RNA genome is copied into viral DNA by reverse transcriptase; viral DNA joins the host DNA and directs production of virus particles (macrophages act as HIV factory). HIV enters helper T cells, replicates and destroys them, so TH cell count falls and the person suffers infections (Mycobacterium, viruses, fungi, Toxoplasma). Diagnosis: ELISA. Prevention: screening blood, disposable needles, condoms, awareness, NACO and NGOs.
items.markingKey: 2 marks infection; 1 mark consequences; 1 mark diagnosis; 1 mark prevention.

items.stem: Which of the following shows the correct sequence of events after HIV infection?
items.answer: virus enters macrophages → helper T cells attacked → immune deficiency
items.markingKey: (b) virus enters macrophages → helper T cells attacked → immune deficiency. Macrophages act as the HIV factory.
options: immune deficiency → helper T cells attacked → virus enters macrophages
virus enters macrophages → helper T cells attacked → immune deficiency
virus enters macrophages → immune deficiency → helper T cells attacked
helper T cells attacked → virus enters macrophages → immune deficiency

items.stem: Which of the following is a disease caused by a helminth?
items.answer: filariasis
items.markingKey: (d) Filariasis is a disease caused by a helminth; the others are not.

items.stem: A type of immunity has these features: by infection or vaccination; slow to develop; body produces its own antibodies. Which type of immunity is it? Give a reason.
items.answer: Active immunity
items.markingKey: 1 mark: active immunity; 1 mark: the features by infection or vaccination; slow to develop; body produces its own antibodies are characteristic of it.

items.stem:
A type of immunity has these features: slow to develop; by infection or vaccination; body produces its own antibodies.
(i) Which type of immunity is it? (1 mark)
(ii) State one more feature you would expect to observe. (1 mark)
(iii) How would the observations differ if it were passive immunity? Give two points. (2 marks)
items.answer: (i) Active immunity (ii) long lasting (iii) immediate protection; ready-made antibodies are given
items.markingKey: (i) active immunity – 1 mark. (ii) any one of: long lasting – 1 mark. (iii) for passive immunity: ready-made antibodies are given; immediate protection; short lived – 1 mark each for any two.

items.stem: Which pathogen causes amoebiasis?
items.answer: Entamoeba histolytica
items.markingKey: (c) Amoebiasis is caused by Entamoeba histolytica; spread by houseflies carry cysts to food and water.

items.stem:
Assertion (A): Sharing needles among drug users is very dangerous.
Reason (R): It can spread HIV and hepatitis B.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
items.markingKey: (a) Infections spread through blood.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem: What is meant by “a benign tumour”?
items.answer: A tumour that remains confined to its original location and does not spread.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: a tumour that remains confined to its original location and does not spread.

items.stem: Arrange the following in the correct sequence of the life cycle of Plasmodium: sporozoites in salivary glands, gametocytes formed in RBCs, sporozoites enter human blood, attack on RBCs. Give a reason.
items.answer: sporozoites enter human blood → attack on RBCs → gametocytes formed in RBCs → sporozoites in salivary glands
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the order sporozoites enter human blood → attack on RBCs → gametocytes formed in RBCs → sporozoites in salivary glands; 1 mark for the reason: Asexual phase in humans and sexual phase in the mosquito.

items.stem:
Assertion (A): MALT constitutes about 50% of the lymphoid tissue in the human body.
Reason (R): The thymus enlarges with age.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: A is true, but R is false.
items.markingKey: (c) A is true. R is false: The thymus is large at birth and keeps reducing in size with age.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem: The following statement is incorrect. Rewrite it correctly and give a reason: “Cannabinoids are obtained from Papaver somniferum.”
items.answer: They are obtained from the inflorescences of Cannabis sativa; opioids come from the poppy.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the corrected statement, 1 mark for the reason: They are obtained from the inflorescences of Cannabis sativa; opioids come from the poppy.

items.stem: Which of the following is a method of cancer treatment?
items.answer: chemotherapy
items.markingKey: (c) Chemotherapy is a method of cancer treatment; the others are not.

items.stem: What type of immunity is provided by antibodies passed to the foetus through the placenta?
items.answer: passive immunity
items.markingKey: (a) Antibodies passed to the foetus through the placenta: passive immunity – ready-made antibodies are received.

items.stem: What is meant by “sporozoites”?
items.answer: The infectious form of Plasmodium that enters the human body through the bite of an infected female Anopheles.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: the infectious form of Plasmodium that enters the human body through the bite of an infected female Anopheles.

items.stem: Arrange the following in the correct sequence of events after HIV infection: viral DNA incorporated into host DNA, new viruses produced, helper T cells attacked, viral RNA copied into DNA by reverse transcriptase. Give a reason.
items.answer: viral RNA copied into DNA by reverse transcriptase → viral DNA incorporated into host DNA → new viruses produced → helper T cells attacked
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the order viral RNA copied into DNA by reverse transcriptase → viral DNA incorporated into host DNA → new viruses produced → helper T cells attacked; 1 mark for the reason: Macrophages act as the HIV factory.

items.stem: Classify each of the following as primary lymphoid organ or secondary lymphoid organ: thymus, Peyer's patches, lymph nodes, bone marrow.
items.answer: thymus – primary lymphoid organ; Peyer's patches – secondary lymphoid organ; lymph nodes – secondary lymphoid organ; bone marrow – primary lymphoid organ.
items.markingKey: ½ mark each: thymus – primary lymphoid organ; Peyer's patches – secondary lymphoid organ; lymph nodes – secondary lymphoid organ; bone marrow – primary lymphoid organ.

items.stem: Give two differences between a benign tumour and a malignant tumour.
items.answer: A benign tumour: confined to original location; cells may be enclosed in a capsule. A malignant tumour: mass of proliferating neoplastic cells; cells starve normal cells of nutrients.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for each correct, paired difference, e.g. a benign tumour – confined to original location; cells may be enclosed in a capsule; a malignant tumour – mass of proliferating neoplastic cells; cells starve normal cells of nutrients.
